paper.title: Black-box optimization of noisy functions with unknown smoothness

settings.name_in_paper: Black-box optimization of a noisy function with unknown smoothness given a hierarchical partitioning
unmapped: Arbitrary measurable domain X with a known hierarchical partitioning (tree with at most K_children children per cell) given to the learner
Local smoothness w.r.t. the partitioning (Assumption 1): f(x) >= f(x*) - nu*rho^h on the depth-h cell containing a global optimum; (nu, rho) unknown to the learner
Learner knows upper bounds nu_max and rho_max on the smoothness parameters
Complexity measured by a partition-dependent near-optimality dimension d(nu, rho)
settings.definition_quote: At each step $t$, an algorithm selects an action $x_t\in\mathcal{X}$ and receives a reward $r_t$, which is a noisy function evaluation such that $r_t =  f(x_t) + \varepsilon_t$, where $\varepsilon_t$ is a bounded noise with $\EEc{\varepsilon_t}{x_t} = 0$. After $n$ evaluations, the algorithm outputs its best guess $x(n)$ ... R_n \eqdef \sup_{x\in \mathcal{X}}f(x)  - f\left(x\left(n\right)\right)

algorithms.name: POO (Parallel Optimistic Optimization)
requires_knowledge_of: K_children (max number of children per cell)

symbols.alpha_c: constant independent of rho_max and nu_max
symbols.D_max: ln(K_children)/ln(1/rho_max), K_children = max number of children per cell
symbols.nu_max: upper bound on nu given to POO
symbols.nu_star: smoothness constant nu of the best parameters (nu_star, rho_star)
symbols.d_nr: near-optimality dimension d(nu, rho) w.r.t. the partitioning

conditions: (nu, rho) verifies Assumption 1 (local smoothness w.r.t. the partitioning)
noise bounded with zero conditional mean
tuning: number of HOO instances N >= (1/2) D_max ln(n/ln n), doubled when needed

results.notes: Noise range not precisely stated ('bounded noise'); proof uses Hoeffding with values in [0,1], mapped to bounded_pm1. alpha_c is an unspecified constant (may depend on the instance through C(nu_star,rho_star)). n is T. Anytime algorithm.
